svg.title: Figure 7-1 · Assumptions of use by subject and status
svg.desc: Cards for the 18 assumptions of use of WP-C-01 §7, grouped as Vehicle ECUs: AOU-01, AOU-02, AOU-03, AOU-04, AOU-05, AOU-10, AOU-12, AOU-16, AOU-17, AOU-18; Installation and maintenance: AOU-08, AOU-09, AOU-13; Driver: AOU-06, AOU-07; Network and back end: AOU-11; Build configuration: AOU-14, AOU-15. Each card shows the ID, the first clause of the assumption, a status pill (AOU-01 Unverified; AOU-02 Unverified; AOU-03 Unverified; AOU-04 Unverified; AOU-05 Unverified; AOU-06 SOTIF-managed; AOU-07 Not started; AOU-08 Partially; AOU-09 Not started; AOU-10 Not started; AOU-11 Design constraint; AOU-12 Unverified; AOU-13 Unverified; AOU-14 Unverified; AOU-15 Unverified; AOU-16 Not started; AOU-17 Unverified; AOU-18 Unverified), where it is credited and the verification approach. None is verified.
svg.text: Figure 7-1 · Assumptions of use by subject and status
The 18 assumptions of §7 grouped by what they assume. No assumption is verified; each needs evidence before it is credited.
The Toyota EPS limits the torque applied for
LKA requests to a level a normal driver can
Credited in: HARA controllability of H-01/H-05
max LKA torque at the wheel, timeout behaviour,
A normal driver can override full LKA torque
with steering force within the controllability
criterion set by CA-01 in WP-C-08 §7
Credited in: HARA C-rating H-01, H-05
Verification: Vehicle measurement with a steering
Driver brake pedal application always produces
braking regardless of ACC commands, and the PCM
The stock PCS/AEB keeps full function with the
Verification: Review of forwarded and blocked
The PCM bounds ACC acceleration and
deceleration requests to its own ACC envelope
The cluster cruise indicator is driven by PCM
state and is not influenced by item TX messages
Credited in: FSC FSR-05.05; independent cue for
When the item brings the vehicle to a
standstill under ACC, the PCM keeps it stopped
and held, without the driver pressing the
brake, for as long as ACC stays engaged, and
does not let it roll or move off
Credited in: WP-C-03 SG-08 safe state (DQ-365 A);
Verification: Vehicle test on the reference Corolla
(DQ-365 option A): forced stop under ACC on level
ground and on a grade at the ODD bound (6 %), with
the hold duration and any time-out measured
The EPS signals every drop of LKA assistance
and the PCM signals every non-execution of ACC
requests, so that neither stops acting on the
item's requests without a fault the item can
Verification: Vehicle tests with forced faults
(WP-V-07). If a test finds a silent drop, a
(c) extended to that case; DQ-360 option B)
The commands the item replaces travel on
classical CAN or ISO CAN FD at the connector
authentication that the item cannot produce
Credited in: Architecture: interception at the
Verification: Configuration review of each vehicle:
bus type and bit rates from the DBC and the opendbc
platform flags (no SecOC on the replaced messages),
confirmed by a bus capture at the harness point
The device is mounted and calibrated according
The vehicle is maintained, unmodified, and has
no active DTCs in the EPS, brake or powertrain
The de-energised harness relay connects the
forward camera to the vehicle CAN without any
Credited in: FSC FSR-07.03; SG-07 safe state
The driver is licensed, attentive, briefed
according to WP-O-03, and keeps their eyes on
During development, only trained safety drivers
operate the item on public roads, under WP-V-07
The comma.ai back end and network are untrusted
The reference build is used with openpilot's
The reference build is used only on camera-ACC
SOTIF-managed / Design constraint (not a verification status)
Verification line in teal: the approach of §7, not a result.
What credits each assumption (hazardous events, goals, TSRs, HWSRs) is shown in WP-T-01 Figure 6 (assumption exposure); this figure groups the §7 table and does not repeat those counts.
